:::{#thm-entropy-quantization}
#### Entropy of a quantized random variable

Let $X$ be a [continuous random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-continuous-rv) whose [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) is continuous,
and whose [entropy](#def-entropy) is a [Riemann integral](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-riemann-integral).
For a bin width $\Delta > 0$,
let $X^\Delta$ be the [discrete random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-discrete-rv) that records the bin of $X$:
$X^\Delta = x_i$ when $i\Delta \le X < (i+1)\Delta$,
where $x_i$ is a point of that bin with $\p(X=x_i)\,\Delta = \P(i\Delta \le X < (i+1)\Delta)$.
Such a point exists because the density is continuous.
Then

$$\entropyf{X^\Delta} + \log \Delta \to \entropyf{X} \quad \text{as } \Delta \to 0.$$

[@cover2006elements, Theorem 8.3.1]

:::

::: proof

By the choice of $x_i$,
the [probability mass](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) of $X^\Delta$ at $x_i$ is $\P(X^\Delta = x_i) = \p(X=x_i)\,\Delta$.
By @thm-entropy-discrete,

$$
\ba
\entropyf{X^\Delta}
&= -\sum_i \p(X=x_i)\,\Delta \log \paren{\p(X=x_i)\,\Delta} && \text{(@thm-entropy-discrete)} \\
&= -\sum_i \Delta\, \p(X=x_i) \log \p(X=x_i) - \sum_i \p(X=x_i)\,\Delta \log \Delta && \text{(log of a product)} \\
&= -\sum_i \Delta\, \p(X=x_i) \log \p(X=x_i) - \log \Delta. && \text{(the masses sum to } 1 \text{)}
\ea
$$

Adding $\log \Delta$ to both sides leaves the first [sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-summation),
which is a [Riemann sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-riemann-sum) for $-\int \p(X=x) \log \p(X=x)\, dx$.
By @thm-entropy-continuous, that integral is $\entropyf{X}$,
and a Riemann sum [converges](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#thm-riemann-general) to its [Riemann integral](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-riemann-integral) as $\Delta \to 0$.

:::
